terms.grammar: adjective; with ad + gerund, the dative, or quī + subjunctive
evidence: Caes. B.G. 2.8.3: locō … opportūnō atque idōneō (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Lael. 62: ad amīcitiam esse idōneus
terms.comment: The everyday word, of things and of people (a person fit or capable for a task).

terms.grammar: adjective; with ad or the dative, of persons always the dative
evidence: Cic. de Or. 1.231: calceī habilēs et aptī ad pedem (Lewis & Short, s.v. apō)
terms.comment: Literally fastened, joined (the participle of an old verb apere); so fitted to something, suitable. It can also mean ready, equipped.

terms.grammar: adjective; with ad or the dative
evidence: Caes. B.G. 3.13: puppēs ad magnitūdinem flūctuum accommodātae (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: A prose word (Lewis & Short), of things made or chosen to fit a purpose.

phrases.latin: apēs, ut ajunt, dēbēmus imitārī, quae vagantur et flōrēs ad mel faciendum idōneōs carpunt
phrases.english: we should copy the bees, as they say, which wander and pick the flowers fit for making honey

phrases.latin: calceī habilēs et aptī ad pedem
phrases.english: shoes that are easy to wear and fit the foot

phrases.latin: Haec vestis ad nūptiās nōn est idōnea.
phrases.english: These clothes aren’t suitable for a wedding.

sources: Lewis & Short: idoneus · Lewis & Short: apo · Lewis & Short: accommodo
